What the numbers say

For the session of Monday, November 16, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (36 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as risk-off. SPY is below its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is down and realised volatility is in the moderate band.

9 of 36 tickers (25%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 15 of 34 (44%) above their 200-day average. Below 30% is the level the model treats as weak breadth, which is enough on its own for a risk-off reading. On the day 4 rose and 32 fell; the median move was −3.06%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Healthcare had the strongest average move at −0.25% and Technology the weakest at −4.99%, a spread of 4.74 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 1.85 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

2 tickers have a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (NVDA, INTC), and 1 at or above 70 (COST). An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-13), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 33% to 25%, and the regime reading changed from mixed to risk-off.
